detail.longDescription: arXiv:2610.09659v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum circuit simulation enables the execution of large-scale quantum algorithms by partitioning qubits across multiple computational nodes. However, an inefficient qubit placement leads to excessive inter-node communication, limiting performance and scalability. This work introduces a framework that computes a communication-aware qubit placement offline, minimizing data exchange among nodes, and selects, before circuit execution, the largest node count whose performance degradation stays below a user-defined threshold. The framework is integrated with the QuEST simulator. Evaluations on synthetic benchmarks and real-world QASMBench circuits show that optimized placements reduce communication and achieve runtime speedups of up to 2.3x over the identity placement, particularly in circuits with sparse, structured interactions. Our results show that qubit placement strongly affects the efficiency of distributed simulation and provide a practical, resource-scalable solution for quantum workload
